# Review packet P2-general_information-01

Priority P2, domain general_information, 9 items. Status of every item: not approved.

**How to review independently:** answer every item below before opening the answer sheet. Then compare, and mark each item ACCEPT / FIX (say what) / REJECT in `decisions.csv` (one row per id). Do not edit the item files; the bank worker applies fixes as draft replacements.

**Check for this domain:** Open the source_url and find the quoted text. Does it support the key exactly, and is the law still current (no amendment)?

## Items

### 1. `CIVIO-B3-GI-DEADLINE-NUMBER-0067`  (both, medium, 30 s)

Under R.A. 6713, when must a covered public employee file the Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN)?

- (A) Within 30 days after assuming office, on or before April 30 every year, and within 30 days after leaving the service
- (B) Within 60 days after assuming office, on or before April 15 every year, and within 60 days after leaving the service
- (C) Within 30 days after assuming office, on or before December 31 every year, and within one year after leaving the service
- (D) Within 15 working days after assuming office, on or before June 30 every year, and only if asked after leaving the service

### 2. `CIVIO-B3-GI-ENV-PRINCIPLE-0011`  (both, easy, 20 s)

- (A) Using any natural resources to support present economic growth
- (B) Compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
- (C) Allowing private companies to operate inside protected areas
- (D) Allowing a country's population to increase over the next decades

## Answer sheet (open only after answering)

### 1. `CIVIO-B3-GI-DEADLINE-NUMBER-0067`: key (A) Within 30 days after assuming office, on or before April 30 every year, and within 30 days after leaving the service

- Why correct: Answer: Within 30 days after assuming office, on or before April 30 every year, and within 30 days after leaving the service. Sec. 8(A) sets three filing points: (a) within 30 days after assumption of office, (b) on or before April 30 of every year thereafter, and (c) within 30 days after separation from the service.
- (B) 60 days is the Sec. 9 divestment period, and April 15 is the income-tax deadline, not the SALN date.
- (C) December 31 is the as-of date of the figures, not the filing deadline; separation filing is 30 days, not one year.
- (D) 15 working days is the Sec. 5(a) reply period for letters; separation filing is mandatory, not on request.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 8(A) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "(a) within thirty (30) days after assumption of office; (b) on or before April 30, of every year thereafter; and (c) within thirty (30) days after separation from the service"
- File: `docs/research/audit/fixes/round-03-baseline-b3-drafts.json`
- Review note: legacy row: no domain solver; key checked by hand sheet (audit/legacy_keys or GI evidence sheet)

### 2. `CIVIO-B3-GI-ENV-PRINCIPLE-0011`: key (B) Compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs

- Why correct: Answer: Compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. The standard definition: meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
- (A) Sustainable development allows resource use; it limits use that harms future generations.
- (C) Private activity is regulated by protected-area law, not excluded by the definition.
- (D) Population growth is not part of the definition.
- Source: Our Common Future (WCED, 1987); R.A. 9003, Sec. 2(c) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2001/ra_9003_2001.html>; quote: "in accordance with ecologically sustainable development principles"
- File: `docs/research/audit/fixes/round-03-baseline-b3-drafts.json`
- Review note: legacy row: no domain solver; key checked by hand sheet (audit/legacy_keys or GI evidence sheet)

### 3. `CIVIO-B3-GI-ENV-PRINCIPLE-0228`: key (D) Water and pollutants move through a drainage area toward a common outlet

- Why correct: Answer: Water and pollutants move through a drainage area toward a common outlet. R.A. 9275 Sec. 5 designates management areas using physiographic units such as watersheds and river basins, because water and its pollutants move through a shared drainage area.
- (A) Watersheds are not factory zones.
- (B) Runoff picks up pollutants; that is why they are managed.
- (C) Watersheds follow terrain, not political boundaries; that is why LGUs must cooperate.
- Source: R.A. 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004), Sec. 5 <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2004/ra_9275_2004.html>; quote: "using appropriate physiographic units such as watershed, river basins or water resources regions"
- File: `docs/research/audit/fixes/round-03-baseline-b3-drafts.json`
- Review note: legacy row: no domain solver; key checked by hand sheet (audit/legacy_keys or GI evidence sheet)

### 4. `CIVIO-B3-GI-ENV-PRINCIPLE-0229`: key (A) They are prohibited and existing ones must be closed or converted

- Why correct: Answer: They are prohibited and existing ones must be closed or converted. Sec. 37 prohibits establishing or operating open dumps and set a conversion/closure schedule; Sec. 48(9) penalizes it.
- (B) No barangay approval makes an open dump lawful under Sec. 37.
- (C) The Act requires closure, not open dumps.
- (D) Sec. 48(6) also prohibits dumping biodegradable materials in flood-prone areas; no exception for biodegradables.
- Source: R.A. 9003, Secs. 3(t), 37, 48(9) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2001/ra_9003_2001.html>; quote: "No open dumps shall be established and operated, nor any practice or disposal of solid waste by any person, including LGUs, which constitutes the use of open dumps for solid wastes, be allowed"
- File: `docs/research/audit/fixes/round-03-baseline-b3-drafts.json`
- Review note: legacy row: no domain solver; key checked by hand sheet (audit/legacy_keys or GI evidence sheet)

### 5. `CIVIO-B3-GI-ENV-PRINCIPLE-0410`: key (D) Preventive action against a serious threat even without full scientific certainty

- Why correct: Answer: Preventive action against a serious threat even without full scientific certainty. R.A. 9729 Sec. 2 names the Precautionary Principle; lack of full scientific certainty is not a reason to postpone preventive measures (see also Rule 20, A.M. No. 09-6-8-SC).
- (A) That is the opposite of precaution.
- (B) That is the polluter-pays principle.
- (C) That distorts common but differentiated responsibilities, a separate Sec. 2 principle.
- Source: R.A. 9729 (Climate Change Act of 2009), Sec. 2 <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2009/ra_9729_2009.html>; quote: "common but differentiated responsibilities and the Precautionary Principle to guide decision-making in climate risk management"
- File: `docs/research/audit/fixes/round-03-baseline-b3-drafts.json`
- Review note: legacy row: no domain solver; key checked by hand sheet (audit/legacy_keys or GI evidence sheet)

### 6. `CIVIO-B3-GI-ENV-PRINCIPLE-0413`: key (B) To conserve biological diversity and maintain ecological processes

- Why correct: Answer: To conserve biological diversity and maintain ecological processes. R.A. 11038 Sec. 2 (amending R.A. 7586 Sec. 2) establishes NIPAS for biologically important areas, to be managed consistently with biological diversity and sustainable development.
- (A) Protected areas are not housing reserves.
- (C) Commercial exploitation is restricted, not the purpose.
- (D) Tourism in protected areas is regulated, not exempt.
- Source: R.A. 7586, Sec. 2, as amended by R.A. 11038, Sec. 2 <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2018/ra_11038_2018.html>; quote: "consistent with the principles of biological diversity and sustainable development"
- File: `docs/research/audit/fixes/round-03-baseline-b3-drafts.json`
- Review note: legacy row: no domain solver; key checked by hand sheet (audit/legacy_keys or GI evidence sheet)

### 7. `CIVIO-B3-GI-ENV-PRINCIPLE-0527`: key (A) Reduce and reuse first, recycle and recover next, dispose last

- Why correct: Answer: Reduce and reuse first, recycle and recover next, dispose last. Sec. 2(c) sets targets for avoidance and volume reduction through source reduction, composting, recycling, re-use and recovery before collection, treatment and disposal.
- (B) Disposal is the last step, not the first.
- (C) Reduction comes before recycling.
- (D) Burning is prohibited (Sec. 48(3); R.A. 8749 Sec. 20 bans incineration).
- Source: R.A. 9003, Sec. 2(c) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2001/ra_9003_2001.html>; quote: "solid waste avoidance and volume reduction through source reduction and waste minimization measures, including composting, recycling, re-use, recovery, green charcoal process, and others, before collection, treatment and disposal"
- File: `docs/research/audit/fixes/round-03-baseline-b3-drafts.json`
- Review note: legacy row: no domain solver; key checked by hand sheet (audit/legacy_keys or GI evidence sheet)

### 8. `CIVIO-B3-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0072`: key (B) A conflict of interest

- Why correct: Answer: A conflict of interest. Her shares give her a financial interest in a supplier whose bid her own office will decide, so her private interest can be affected by her official duty (Sec. 3(i)). The item does not depend on whether 20% makes her a "substantial stockholder" (Sec. 3(f): enough shares to elect a director). Sec. 7(a) bars any financial or material interest in a transaction requiring her office's approval, and Sec. 9 requires divestment when a conflict arises.
- (A) Sec. 4(A)(c) concerns favors to relatives; here the interest is the officer's own.
- (C) Divestment (Sec. 3(j)) is the cure for the conflict, not its name.
- (D) Sec. 7(b) outside employment concerns working for a regulated firm; owning shares is not employment.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 3(i) and Sec. 9 <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: ""Conflict of interest" arises when a public official or employee is a member of a board, an officer, or a substantial stockholder of a private corporation or owner or has a substantial interest in a business, and the interest of such corporation or business, or his rights or duties therein, may be opposed to or affected by the faithful performance of official duty"
- File: `docs/research/audit/fixes/round-03-baseline-b3-drafts.json`
- Review note: legacy row: no domain solver; key checked by hand sheet (audit/legacy_keys or GI evidence sheet)

### 9. `CIVIO-B3-GI-SCENARIO-APPLY-0395`: key (B) The position is strictly confidential or on the mayor's personal staff, coterminous with him

- Why correct: Answer: The position is strictly confidential or on the mayor's personal staff, coterminous with him. Sec. 4(A)(c) bars undue favors to relatives except appointments to strictly confidential positions or to personal staff whose terms are coterminous with the official.
- (A) Eligibility is a separate requirement; it does not create the statutory exception.
- (C) Serving without pay is not an exception in the Act.
- (D) Publicity does not cure an undue favor.
- Source: R.A. 6713, Sec. 4(A)(c) <https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1989/ra_6713_1989.html>; quote: "except with respect to appointments of such relatives to positions considered strictly confidential or as members of their personal staff whose terms are coterminous with theirs"
- File: `docs/research/audit/fixes/round-03-baseline-b3-drafts.json`
